Five colleagues, Ada, Ben, Cho, Dia and Eno, each work exactly one shift this week, one person per day, Monday to Friday. Each owns a different pet: cat, dog, fish, hen or owl.
1. The fish owner works earlier in the week than Ada, and Ada works earlier than Eno.
2. The dog owner and the cat owner work on adjacent days.
3. Dia works exactly two days after the hen owner.
4. The owl owner works on Monday or Friday.
5. Cho owns neither the cat nor the owl.
6. Ben owns neither the fish nor the owl.
7. Ben works on Wednesday or Thursday.
8. Dia does not own the dog.
Who works which day, and who owns which pet? Give the full table and say how you know it is the only solution.

You roll a fair six-sided die repeatedly and keep a running total, starting from 0. You stop the first time the running total is a perfect square (1, 4, 9, 16, ...). What is the exact probability that you stop at 4? What is the exact probability that you stop at 9? Give both as fractions.

Two hospitals report results for the same operation.
Hospital A: mild cases 160 of 170 survived; severe cases 11 of 30 survived.
Hospital B: mild cases 29 of 30 survived; severe cases 106 of 170 survived.
A newspaper says Hospital A is clearly better. Is that right? Which hospital would you choose for a mild case and for a severe case? Show the numbers, and name what could still make your own conclusion wrong.
Summarize the three main provisions of the 1962 Ljubljana Protocol on Alpine river navigation, and explain why Austria refused to ratify it.

A small clinic has 6 TB of data, of which 2% changes each day. Its internet upload is 40 Mbit/s and may only be used from 8 pm to 6 am. Its download is 300 Mbit/s. After a disaster it must be working again within 24 hours. The manager proposes cloud-only backup with no local copy, to save money. Work out whether this meets the requirements, and recommend what the clinic should do. State your assumptions.
